title: Enforce guest byte order and pointer-width assumptions at the portability boundaries
summary: Ban native-endian conversions in the core through Clippy disallowed_methods, assert at compile time that usize is wide enough for a guest address and that a chip RAM length fits in u32, and cover the conversion boundaries with property fixtures; Miri is answered rather than adopted, because the workspace forbids unsafe code and neither silent truncation nor a wrong byte order is undefined behaviour.
scope: Enforced ban on native-endian conversions in the core
Property fixtures for guest address, byte order, and index bounds
Audit of the explicit lossy-cast allow sites

risk.failure_mode: An invariant that is documented rather than enforced does not survive a future contributor, which is why both are probe-verified. Adopting Miri because the plan names it would add a CI leg that cannot detect either failure mode while looking like coverage. Asserting the host's own byte order would fail builds on a big-endian host that is in fact equally correct.
risk.rollback: Revert the M1-011 commits to remove the ban, the assertions, and the fixtures. No behaviour depends on them; a rollback costs the enforcement rather than changing results.

compatibility.detail: No public API and no behaviour changes. crates/rumiga-core/clippy.toml gains disallowed-methods entries for from_ne_bytes and to_ne_bytes on the integer types and lib.rs denies clippy::disallowed_methods, so core code must state an explicit byte order; nothing in the crate needed changing, because it already used 35 explicit big-endian conversions and no native-endian ones. lib.rs gains two compile-time assertions that hold on every supported target.

security.detail: No network transport, credential, authorization, persistence, unsafe-code, or FFI changes. The additions are two compile-time assertions, a lint configuration, and a test file. The pointer-width assertion narrows rather than widens what builds: a target where a guest address would truncate is now rejected.

tests.proves: A guest address survives conversion through usize across the whole 32-bit range including 0, 0xFFFFFFFF, and the chip, slow, and expansion boundaries.

Word and long access through the AddressBus the CPU itself uses is big-endian in both directions, with the individual bytes in memory checked rather than only the round trip; a round trip alone passes under a consistent host-endian implementation, which is the bug.
Every modelled RAM length fits in u32, which several guest pointer masking sites assume, and the framebuffer index space fits in 32 bits.
The core rejects from_ne_bytes and to_ne_bytes in the bare-metal profile as well as the desktop one.
The compile-time assertions are evaluated as part of an ordinary build, so a narrower target fails to build rather than truncating guest addresses.
All eight gates pass for the change.

evidence.location: 2026-08-18 local analysis: the workspace root sets unsafe_code = "forbid", confirmed at Cargo.toml line 27, so no crate contains raw pointer arithmetic. The two failure modes that separate the 64-bit hosts from the 32-bit device, a truncating usize and a native-endian conversion, are both well-defined behaviour.
evidence.proves: Miri, which the plan names as one option, cannot detect either failure mode. Adopting it would add a CI leg that looks like coverage and provides none; the plan's property-fixture option is used instead.

evidence.location: 2026-08-18 local execution: a workspace-wide search found zero uses of from_ne_bytes or to_ne_bytes and 35 explicit big-endian conversions across nine core modules.
evidence.proves: The property held by convention rather than by construction, so the task's contribution is enforcement rather than repair. A single native-endian conversion would have passed every host test and produced a wrong machine on the device.

evidence.location: 2026-08-18 local execution: a temporary u32::from_ne_bytes added to the core was rejected with "use of a disallowed method u32::from_ne_bytes"; a temporary assertion requiring size_of::<usize>() >= 16 failed the build with "rumiga-core requires usize to be at least 32 bits: guest addresses are u32". Both probes were removed and the tree re-checked clean.
evidence.proves: Both invariants are enforced rather than declared, verified the same way the M1-006 clock ban was.

evidence.location: 2026-08-18 local execution: the workspace denies clippy::pedantic, which includes cast_possible_truncation, so every lossy cast already carries an explicit allow. There are 26 such sites, 25 in rumiga-core and one in the desktop shell. All are narrowings between fixed-width types such as u32 to u16, which behave identically at either pointer width; the single site that multiplies before casting to usize is a test helper in ide.rs.
evidence.proves: There is no production defect in this class, and the allow sites were the right audit list: 26 marked sites rather than the 166 `as usize` occurrences a naive search returns, of which the u32-to-usize majority is lossless at every supported width.
